title: How to align the IRS in Microsoft Flight Simulator | MSFS A-Z (Letter I)
description:
Master the Inertial Reference System (IRS) and ADIRU in Microsoft Flight Simulator and eliminate alignment faults forever. Learn how laser gyroscopes track Earth's rotation, why modern checklists tell you to skip the ALIGN switch, and how to properly initialize cold-and-dark airliners in the PMDG 737, Fenix A320, and Boeing 777.

Powering up an airliner from cold and dark leaves your primary flight displays blind with zero attitude, horizon, or map data. In this episode of Microsoft Flight Simulator A to Z (Letter I), we break down how the IRS and ADIRU use Earth rate sensing to establish orientation without relying on GPS satellites.

You will learn the mechanics behind laser ring gyroscopes, why your aircraft can sense latitude but requires manual FMC longitude entry, and the critical difference between the ALIGN and NAV switch positions. We cover the pre-flight three-step rule to avoid parking brake alignment faults, the 30-second quick alignment procedure, polar calibration cycles, and how triple-redundant inertial units vote against sensor drift and in-flight failures.
